A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TS-RAG study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching content moved between sections.

before.justification: V3 reports original forecasting results on seven benchmarks, component ablations, retrieval case studies, and inference-time measurements in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains those original results and adds retrieval-distance experiments and an analysis relating dataset characteristics to forecasting improvements.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.3 retain the knowledge-base construction, default Euclidean retrieval, projector, ARM architecture, frozen backbones, training objectives, and inference procedure. The alternative retrieval distances are evaluated as ablation variants.

E1.justification: The Chronos-derived pretraining data and seven forecasting benchmarks are unchanged. The new analyses use subsets of the existing ETT and Exchange Rate datasets without introducing new task requirements or domains.

E2.justification: V4 Table 11 adds cosine-similarity and raw-series DTW retrieval variants as comparators to default Euclidean retrieval and forecasting without RAG. The established TSFM and RAF comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New Appendix B.5 evaluates cosine similarity on Chronos embeddings and DTW on raw sequences. Appendix D introduces dataset-level characteristic aggregation and comparison with MSE gains. Existing splits, forecasting horizons, training settings, and MSE/MAE evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 adds retrieval-distance sensitivity testing and an analysis of which dataset characteristics accompany larger gains. Existing ablations and case studies are retained; the lookback-length study moves from Appendix B.4 to Section 4.3 without new results.

E5.justification: Appendix D newly estimates Pearson correlations between dataset characteristics and MSE improvements across four ETT datasets. Neither version reports forecasting-run uncertainty, and the new correlations have no confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All matched existing tables retain their numerical results. V4 Table 11 adds cosine and DTW scores, including ETTm1 MSE of 0.2906 and 0.3100, respectively. Table 13 adds dataset descriptors and correlations of 0.70, -0.55, -0.65, and -0.19 with MSE gains.

T1.justification: New Appendix D introduces quantitative definitions for its analysis, including volatility as standard deviation divided by sequence mean and a stationarity proxy based on first-difference variance. The method's Equations (1)-(12) remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: retrieval-augmented zero-shot forecasting through ARM, improved generalization and interpretability, and improvements up to 6.84% across seven benchmarks.

C2.justification: V4 interprets the distance experiments as supporting embedding-based retrieval over raw-series DTW. Appendix D adds the interpretation that strong temporal dependencies and relatively stable patterns favor TS-RAG. The existing modality and application limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: V4's abstract newly supplies a repository address for code and data. The new appendices describe where retrieval distances are computed and how dataset characteristics are aggregated. Existing optimizer, hardware, training-time, and implementation disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds seven cited works covering application examples, newer LLM forecasting research, and a foundation-model tutorial/survey. It also connects its new retrieval findings to the already cited RATD work. The central positioning against TSFMs and RAF is retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section sequence are retained. Changes include moving the lookback discussion into Section 4.3, adding appendix subsections and overview explanation, updating an author's name and affiliation, adding acknowledgements, and correcting headings.

P2.justification: V4 adds overview Figure 1 and Tables 11 and 13. The earlier lookback Table 9 becomes main-text Table 3; existing figures and tables are retained with relocation, renumbering, and limited formatting changes.

improvement.justification: The new distance ablation strengthens evidence for the retrieval design, while the overview figure and code/data access information improve clarity and reproducibility. The gains are limited: the main results are unchanged, and Appendix D's correlations cover only four datasets without uncertainty estimates.
